title: Submit vessel incident reports
summary: This page provides instructions on how to report a vessel incident that occurs in NSW navigable water, depending on whether the vessel is recreational or commercial.
intro:
If a boating accident occurs in any port or navigable water in NSW, the master of the vessel must:

If you need help, alert search and rescue services.

Follow the reporting procedures after the incident within the timeframe required for a recreational or commercial vessel.
who_can_apply: The master of a vessel that has been involved in an accident in any port or navigable water in NSW.
what_you_need: The time, place, and nature of the accident.
The name and registration number of the vessels involved (if available).
The name and address of every person who was concerned with, or witnessed, the accident (if available).
Details of any injury or damage resulting from the accident.
Your boat driver's licence or Certificate of Competency details.
For recreational reports: The 'Vessel incident report – PDF' form and supporting documents.
For commercial reports: Completion of the online Incident report (AMSA Form 19) and the online Incident alert (AMSA Form 18).
contact: For further information and assistance with completing the report call 13 12 36.

faqs.q: What should I do if a boating accident happens?
faqs.a: If a boating accident occurs, the master of the vessel must first alert search and rescue services. After the incident, you must follow the required reporting procedures.

faqs.q: How do I report a recreational vessel incident?
faqs.a: You must download the 'Vessel incident report – PDF' form, complete it, attach supporting documents, and then post or email the report using the contact details provided on the form.

faqs.q: How do I report a commercial vessel incident?
faqs.a: For commercial vessels, you must complete the online Incident report (AMSA Form 19) and the online Incident alert (AMSA Form 18), following the prompts to submit both reports.
